title: Triple pathological findings in a surgically amenable patient with mesial temporal lobe epilepsy☆
case_prompt:
A 55-year-old right-handed woman presented with a history of medication-refractory seizures beginning at age 47. Her typical events consisted of staring, lip smacking, unresponsiveness, asymmetric posturing without head or eye deviation, and occasional secondary generalization lasting 3–5 minutes, followed by prolonged postictal confusion. Seizures clustered every 2–3 months, mostly during sleep, despite trials of levetiracetam, lacosamide, and lamotrigine. Neurologic examination was unremarkable.

Brain MRI revealed a 6.5×3.6 cm lobulated, nonenhancing mass in the left quadrigeminal plate cistern extending into the cerebellar vermis and tail of the left hippocampus. On MRI, the lesion was hypointense on T1 and ADC, hyperintense on T2, diffusion-weighted, and FLAIR images, indicating restricted diffusion. The left hippocampus was small with T2 hyperintensity consistent with mesial temporal sclerosis.

Neuropsychological testing showed average cognition with mildly impaired memory lateralizing to the left. Wada testing demonstrated left-hemisphere language dominance and bilateral memory capacity. Long-term video-EEG captured multiple stereotyped seizures with oral automatisms arising from the left anterior-midtemporal region and rhythmic theta activity at onset; interictal EEG showed frequent left anterior-midtemporal slowing and occasional sharp waves, consistent with a hippocampal seizure pattern.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Dermoid cyst — considered among intracranial cystic lesions but excluded by restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging “Differential diagnoses include dermoid cysts, arachnoid cysts, low-grade and cystic astrocytomas, dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumors (DNET), ganglioglioma, oligodendroglioma, and inflammatory cysts. Since epidermoids will show restricted diffusion on MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging may assist with the diagnosis preoperatively.”
2. Arachnoid cyst — listed as a mimic of epidermoid cysts but lacks restricted diffusion characteristic “Differential diagnoses include dermoid cysts, arachnoid cysts … Since epidermoids will show restricted diffusion on MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging may assist with the diagnosis preoperatively.”
3. Low-grade and cystic astrocytomas — included in the differential but these tumors typically do not show the marked diffusion restriction seen here “Differential diagnoses include … low-grade and cystic astrocytomas … Since epidermoids will show restricted diffusion on MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging may assist with the diagnosis preoperatively.”
4. Dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor (DNET) — can present as a cortical cystic lesion but does not show diffusion restriction “Differential diagnoses include … dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumors (DNET) … Since epidermoids will show restricted diffusion on MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging may assist with the diagnosis preoperatively.”
5. Ganglioglioma — part of the differential for cystic temporal lesions but lacks the ADC hypointensity of this lesion “Differential diagnoses include … ganglioglioma … Since epidermoids will show restricted diffusion on MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging may assist with the diagnosis preoperatively.”
6. Oligodendroglioma — may appear cystic but does not display the diffusion restriction characteristic of epidermoid cysts “Differential diagnoses include … oligodendroglioma … Since epidermoids will show restricted diffusion on MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging may assist with the diagnosis preoperatively.”
7. Inflammatory cysts — can mimic intracranial cystic masses but are not diffusion-restricting like epidermoid cysts “Differential diagnoses include … inflammatory cysts. Since epidermoids will show restricted diffusion on MRI, diffusion-weighted imaging may assist with the diagnosis preoperatively.”
